def: Retrieval that embeds queries and passages as vectors and returns the passages whose vectors are closest to the query's.
A list of real numbers produced by a neural network to represent a piece of text so that similar texts get nearby vectors.
A model with separate query and passage encoders whose vectors are compared by dot product, so passage vectors can be computed offline.
A training loss that pulls matching pairs together and pushes non-matching pairs apart in vector space.
A softmax contrastive loss that asks the model to pick the true positive out of one positive and many negatives.
A constant that divides similarities before the softmax; small values sharpen the distribution and focus training on the hardest negatives.
Using the positive passages of the other queries in a training batch as negatives, giving B squared comparisons from B pairs.
A passage that looks relevant to the query (high lexical or embedding score) but is not, used to teach fine distinctions.
A passage treated as non-relevant in training because it was never labelled, although it actually answers the query.
Turning a transformer's per-token outputs into one vector per text, by taking the first token, averaging, or taking the last token.
The dot product of two vectors after scaling each to length 1, measuring the angle between them.
Continuing to train a pretrained embedding model on your own query and passage pairs, followed by re-embedding the whole corpus.
